test_title: PYST 2: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - GA (Held On 25 Jul, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: gk
question: Which of the following is NOT a reason for a fiscal deficit?

options.text: High government expenditure on welfare schemes
Surplus in the balance of payments

solution:
The correct answer is __**Surplus in the balance of payments**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fiscal Deficit** is defined as the excess of the **government's total expenditure** over its **total revenue**, excluding **borrowings**, during a specific **financial year**. It indicates the total **borrowing requirements** of the government.
 
• **High government expenditure on welfare schemes:** When the **government** increases spending on **social welfare**, **subsidies**, and **infrastructure** without a corresponding increase in **revenue**, the gap between income and expenditure widens. ***Hence, this statement is a correct reason for a fiscal deficit.***
 
• **Reduction in tax revenue:** A decline in **tax collection**, whether due to **economic slowdown**, **tax evasion**, or **tax cuts** implemented by the **Ministry of Finance**, reduces the **government's income**. This shortfall directly contributes to the **budgetary gap**. ***Hence, this statement is a correct reason for a fiscal deficit.***
 
• **Increase in public borrowings:** While **borrowing** is a way to finance a **deficit**, high levels of **public debt** lead to massive **interest payments** in subsequent years. These interest payments are a form of **revenue expenditure** that further inflates the **fiscal deficit**. ***Hence, this statement is a correct reason for a fiscal deficit.***
 
• **Surplus in the balance of payments:** This occurs when a **country's** total **exports** and **capital inflows** exceed its **imports** and **capital outflows**. This is an **international trade** metric and does not represent a shortfall in the **domestic budget** of the **government**. ***Hence, this statement is NOT a reason for a fiscal deficit.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Revenue Deficit:** This refers to the excess of **revenue expenditure** over **revenue receipts**. It signifies that the **government** is unable to cover its **day-to-day operational expenses** (like salaries and pensions) from its regular income.
 
• **Primary Deficit:** This is the **Fiscal Deficit** minus the **interest payments** on previous **borrowings**. It shows how much the **government** needs to borrow to meet its **current year** expenses, excluding the burden of **past debt**.
 
• **Fiscal Policy:** In **India**, fiscal policy is the tool used by the **Union Government** to monitor and influence the **economy** by adjusting **spending levels** and **tax rates**. It is managed primarily through the **Union Budget** presented every **February**.
 
• **Sources of Revenue:** The **government** earns through **tax revenue** (Direct taxes like **Income Tax** and **Corporate Tax**, and Indirect taxes like **GST**) and **non-tax revenue** (interest receipts, **dividends** from **PSUs**, and **external grants**).
 
• **Capital Receipts:** These include **recoveries of loans**, **disinvestment** of **Public Sector Undertakings**, and **borrowings**. Unlike **revenue receipts**, these either create a **liability** or reduce the **assets** of the **government**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **FRBM Act, 2003:** The **Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act** was enacted to ensure **inter-generational equity** in **fiscal management** and long-term **macro-economic stability**. It aimed to limit the **fiscal deficit** to **3% of the GDP**.
 
• **Deficit Financing:** To bridge the **fiscal gap**, the **government** may borrow from the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** or the **public**. If the **RBI** prints new **currency** to fund the **deficit**, it can lead to high **inflation** in the **economy**.
 
• **Impact of High Deficit:** Persistent **fiscal deficits** can lead to a **debt trap**, **crowding out** of **private investment** (as the **government** consumes most of the **market credit**), and a decrease in the **sovereign credit rating** of the **country**.
 
• **Grants-in-aid:** Under **Article 275** of the **Constitution of India**, the **Union** provides **grants** to **states**, which is a major **expenditure** item that impacts the **fiscal deficit** of the **Central Government**.
</ul
